assessments.rationale: Using recycled aluminum significantly reduces the manufacturing environmental footprint (m) compared to virgin materials, requiring up to 95% less energy in production (g). Furthermore, machining aluminum avoids the generation and release of microplastics and nanoplastics (p) during the trimming, deburring, and finishing stages, which is a major concern with polymer-based housings.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use Phase, as an aluminum housing increases the weight of the screwdriver, potentially causing user fatigue and increasing energy consumption during transport.

assessments.rationale: Snap-fits allow for rapid, low-energy assembly, minimizing resource consumption in production (g). They eliminate the need for secondary fasteners or adhesives, thereby reducing manufacturing waste (r) and avoiding VOC emissions to air (q) associated with solvent-based bonding agents.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Repairability and End-of-Life stages; snap-fits are prone to shearing or breaking during disassembly, which prevents easy repair and can lead to entire components being discarded.

assessments.rationale: Brushed motors have a much simpler design and manufacturing process. They avoid the use of complex rare-earth magnets (neodymium) and intricate stator winding processes, which drastically reduces the upstream manufacturing environmental footprint (m), water and energy consumption in production (g), and toxic emissions to soil and water from rare-earth mining (q).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use Phase, as brushed motors have lower energy efficiency, shorter lifespans due to brush wear, and generate carbon dust during operation.

assessments.rationale: Passive cooling relies on natural airflow and integrated housing vents, requiring no additional components. This eliminates the energy, water, and resources needed to manufacture auxiliary fans or heat sinks (g), minimizes production waste (r), and lowers the overall manufacturing footprint (m) of the bill of materials.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use Phase, as passive cooling limits heat dissipation, potentially leading to thermal throttling, reduced motor efficiency, and a shorter product lifespan under heavy loads.

assessments.rationale: A monolithic design consolidates components, reducing the number of connectors, internal wiring, and structural frames. This minimizes assembly complexity, reduces energy consumption on the production line (g), lowers the manufacturing footprint (m), and significantly reduces material scrap and waste generated during production (r).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Directly conflicts with the Repairability and Maintenance stage, as a monolithic architecture makes it extremely difficult to replace individual failed components (like a single gear or switch), forcing the replacement of the entire tool.

assessments.rationale: An integrated battery design simplifies the internal layout, requiring fewer housing materials, no separate battery casing, and no complex latching mechanisms. This reduces the consumption of plastic and metal resources in production (g), lowers the manufacturing footprint (m), and generates less production waste (r) compared to manufacturing a separate, robust removable battery pack.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use Phase and End-of-Life stages; integrated batteries cannot be easily swapped when depleted or replaced when degraded, shortening the product's useful life and making safe recycling extraction difficult.
